purpose: Immutable supervised baseline. Every Phase-3 (GRPO/RLVR) result is reported against this record. Nothing here may be retrained or overwritten.
auditor_note: Never used in any reward. Scores final candidates only, so that a reported improvement cannot be an artifact of THESE FOUR PARTICULAR reward models' idiosyncrasies. It is held out of the reward PATH; it is NOT statistically independent of the reward models. scripts/run_splits.py builds five independent random 80/20 splits of the same corpus, not a partitioning k-fold, so split 4 trains on a random 80% of the same LamaLab Tg data and shares ~80% of its training set with each reward model in expectation, and its own held-out 20% is not held out from the reward ensemble. A reward hack that exploits a genuinely data-sparse region of chemical space would fool all five models identically, because all five are sparse there. The check is real and worth having; it cannot establish that a Tg claim is true.
auditor_process_note: By default the auditor is held out of the training process entirely, not merely out of the reward path: scripts/train_grpo.py's build_drift_monitor does not open, verify, or construct the split-4 checkpoint unless --drift-auditor is passed. This is stronger than 'loaded but never consulted for a reward' -- sigma (ensemble disagreement) is itself optimized against by the Tg confidence weight, so it cannot double as a trustworthy drift diagnostic, and the auditor gap was the proposed check on that; but auditor_note's ~80%-shared-training-data limitation gives it only weak power to catch what sigma cannot, so never opening it by default is preferred over loading it unused. max-Tanimoto similarity monitoring (polyt5.rl.DriftMonitor's other half) needs no auditor and stays on. --drift-auditor opts back into the auditor-gap half: polyt5.rl.DriftMonitor then loads it for spec 4.4's logging only -- GRPOTrainer holds the monitor in an attribute of its own, never passes it to the reward arm, and only writes its output into the step stats. tests/test_rl_drift.py pins that a step's rewards, advantages and loss are identical with and without a monitor attached.

evaluation_protocol.note: Phase-3 arms must be evaluated identically.

success_criterion: An RLVR arm succeeds only if it beats arm_b on the metric it optimized AND the gain survives scoring by the auditor. 'Beats' means, on BOTH scorings, an improvement of at least the arm's pre-registered min_margin AND a 95% bootstrap confidence interval over candidates that excludes zero; and only if the arm was sampled at arm_b's temperature and top_p, since a different sampling point makes the row incomparable on every column. See pre_registered_metrics and success_criterion_statistics. When an arm has been trained at more than one seed, see success_criterion_across_seeds for the second, independent criterion that must ALSO hold.
success_criterion_across_seeds: The bootstrap above captures sampling noise WITHIN one run's candidates; it says nothing about RUN-TO-RUN variance from training the same arm again at a different seed, so two arms differing by a few percent may differ only by seed luck. For an arm trained at N>1 seeds, its ACROSS-SEED criterion has TWO clauses, both required, computed only over seeds sampled at arm_b's own operating point (a seed trained at a different temperature/top_p is excluded from the mean/spread AND the verdict, never averaged in and then separately refused): (1) MEAN -- the arm's across-seed MEAN of its optimized metric (mean over its N per-seed row values, both the ensemble-scored and auditor-scored columns) must beat arm_b's own (single-run) value of the same metric by at least the SAME pre-registered min_margin used above, no separate margin; (2) UNANIMITY -- EVERY individual seed's own value must ALSO clear that same min_margin on its own, not just the mean. Unanimity exists because margin-only on the mean can pass on seeds that disagree about the sign entirely (e.g. per-seed deltas {+0.09, +0.01, -0.04} against min_margin=0.02 give a passing mean of +0.02 while one seed actually lost to arm_b) -- it is distribution-free, needs no assumed sampling distribution at n=1-3, and is exactly what 'not seed luck' means operationally. A seed-level bootstrap or a mean +/- sd/sqrt(n) guard were both considered and rejected: at n=3 the minimum attainable one-sided sign-test p-value is 0.125 (can never reject at 0.05), and an sd/sqrt(n) guard implies a sampling distribution three points cannot support -- both would be statistical theatre. The run-to-run spread (sample standard deviation across seeds) is reported alongside every such comparison, informationally, not as a third gate. An arm measured at exactly ONE seed has no run-to-run spread to report -- scripts/compare_arms.py's matrix states this explicitly ('1 seed'), never as a spread of 0, which would falsely claim a repeat-run agreement that was never measured, and unanimity over one seed reduces to that seed's own margin check. Computed by scripts/compare_arms.py's compute_seed_aggregates(); recorded in summary.json's seed_aggregates block (also carries the seed count actually observed per arm) and appended to matrix.md as a second table. Structural metrics (see structural_metrics) keep Ruling D's N/A auditor clause across seeds too, for the identical reason: comparing a value against itself would manufacture a pass out of a tautology. combined_success additionally requires every contributing seed's OWN per-candidate bootstrap-based success (the per-row column above) to also be true, so a single field exists that has already checked within-run sampling noise, the across-seed mean, and across-seed unanimity together; across_seed_success and success remain reported separately alongside it precisely because they answer different questions and neither should be read as having silently absorbed the other.
control_arm_note: A fifth arm, 'control' (see src/polyt5/rewards/composite.py's ControlArm), trains against reward drawn uniformly at random from [0, 1), independent of the candidate's content entirely -- no validity gate, no chemistry read at all. It is deliberately absent from pre_registered_metrics below: it optimizes NOTHING, so scripts/compare_arms.py's ARM_METRIC has no entry for it and its matrix row's success/across_seed_success columns are always None/N-A, exactly like arm_a/arm_b's. Its purpose is diagnostic, not competitive: if training against pure noise still moves a reported metric (PV rate, diversity, property MAE, ...), that is evidence an apparent improvement in one of the four real arms is not, by itself, attributable to that arm's reward design -- it would need to be shown to exceed what optimizing pure noise already produces through RL mechanics alone (entropy change, KL drift, sampling shift).

pre_registered_metrics._note: The metric each RLVR arm is judged on is fixed HERE, before any arm is trained, so that it cannot be chosen after seeing results. scripts/compare_arms.py's ARM_METRIC must match this record exactly; it asserts so at run time and tests/test_compare_arms.py fails if the two disagree. Each metric is the mean of a per-candidate quantity over the FULL raw rollout batch (gated candidates included in the denominator) except property_mae, which is survivor-only -- which is precisely why property_mae is reported but is not any arm's success metric.

accuracy.why: C1's reward IS mean(closeness x confidence) over the full batch. property_mae is unweighted, unclipped and computed only over PV survivors, so a policy can move the two in opposite directions; it stays in the matrix as an informative off-diagonal column, not as C1's success metric.

validity.why: C2's reward IS 'cleared the full SV->TSD->DD->PV cascade'. Structural: no predictor is involved, so the auditor clause does not apply (see structural_metrics).

composite.why: C3's reward is w_tg*r_tg + w_pv*pv_pass + w_novelty*novel; no pre-existing aggregate column captures the joint, so it is scored with the arm object itself.

constraint.why: C4's reward is a conjunction over (|Tg-target| <= tolerance) AND (SA <= sa_max) AND novel AND ensemble-backed; again no pre-existing aggregate captures the joint.

success_criterion_statistics.test: percentile bootstrap over candidates, resampling each arm's per-candidate metric values independently
success_criterion_statistics.rule: beats_arm_b requires (delta >= min_margin) AND (bootstrap CI lower bound > 0), where delta is signed so that positive always means better. survives_audit applies the identical rule to the auditor-scored column. success = beats_arm_b AND survives_audit AND sampling_matches_arm_b.
success_criterion_statistics.why: A bare inequality on point estimates from one generation seed records an 0.1 K win as success = True, indistinguishable from sampling noise: arm_a and arm_b differ by 3.6 K and MAE sampling error on ~840 survivors at RMSE ~44 K is order 1.5 K. Requiring both a minimum effect size and a CI that excludes zero must be fixed BEFORE the runs or it is post-hoc metric selection.
success_criterion_statistics.across_seed_rule: No bootstrap: across_seed_beats_arm_b requires (across-seed mean delta >= min_margin), same min_margin and sign convention as beats_arm_b above, computed ONLY over seeds whose sampling_matches_arm_b is true (a mismatched seed is excluded from the mean/spread as well as the verdict). across_seed_survives_audit applies the identical rule to the auditor-scored column, or is the literal N/A note for structural_metrics. across_seed_success = across_seed_beats_arm_b AND across_seed_survives_audit AND (sampling_matches_arm_b true for EVERY one of the arm's seeds, unknown/None and false both refusing the verdict but recorded as distinct reasons -- see sampling_mismatch_seeds/sampling_unknown_sampling_seeds). across_seed_unanimous applies the identical per-seed min_margin check to EVERY individual seed's own delta rather than the mean, on both predictor columns, gated by the same sampling-match requirement; see success_criterion_across_seeds for why. combined_success = across_seed_success AND across_seed_unanimous AND (every contributing seed's own per-candidate bootstrap success is true). See success_criterion_across_seeds for the full rationale.

amendments.what: Added pre_registered_metrics, structural_metrics and success_criterion_statistics; changed accuracy's metric from property_mae to accuracy_score; corrected auditor_note's independence claim.
amendments.why: Final whole-branch review findings B2, S3, S4 and S9. Made before any arm was trained: no RLVR result existed, exists, or influenced any of these choices. The measured baseline numbers above (checkpoint hashes, 5-split metrics, arm_a/arm_b sampling results) are unchanged.

amendments.what: Changed scripts/train_grpo.py's default drift-monitoring behaviour: the held-out split-4 auditor is no longer loaded by default -- build_drift_monitor does not open, verify, or construct its checkpoint unless the new --drift-auditor flag is passed. max-Tanimoto similarity monitoring, which needs no auditor, remains on by default. Rewrote auditor_process_note accordingly.
amendments.why: Sigma (ensemble disagreement) is itself optimized against by the Tg reward's confidence weight, so it cannot be trusted as a drift diagnostic; the auditor gap was the proposed check on that, but split 4 shares ~80% of its training data with each reward model and so has only weak power against corpus-wide error. Given that limited power, holding split 4 out of the training PROCESS entirely by default is a strictly stronger containment guarantee than loading it unused. A genuinely independent group-contribution oracle is being built separately to fill the auditor's intended role. Made before any arm was trained: no RLVR result existed, exists, or influenced this choice. The measured baseline numbers above are unchanged.

amendments.what: Added a fifth, negative-control arm ('control' -- see control_arm_note) and multi-seed support: added success_criterion_across_seeds and success_criterion_statistics.across_seed_rule, naming the across-seed criterion scripts/compare_arms.py's compute_seed_aggregates() applies once an arm has been trained at more than one seed. pre_registered_metrics, structural_metrics and the existing per-candidate success_criterion_statistics are unchanged -- the across-seed criterion is a SECOND, additional check, not a replacement, and reuses each arm's existing min_margin.
amendments.why: Neither addition can distinguish 'this reward design worked' from 'any perturbation of this model changes the metrics' on its own: control is the check that RL mechanics alone (entropy change, KL drift, sampling shift) do not already move the reported metrics without any informative reward at all, and the across-seed criterion is the check that a real arm's apparent win is not just seed luck from a single training run. Made before any arm was trained to completion: no RLVR result existed, exists, or influenced either addition. The measured baseline numbers above (checkpoint hashes, 5-split metrics, arm_a/arm_b sampling results) are unchanged.
